endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Permitted Uses and Disclosures: Must be limited to defined functions (e.g., data hosting, analytics).

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: As part of this step, the team should identify documentation regarding how, from what source(s), and under what circumstances data elements were acquired for the AI solution (including manner and mechanism of consent where appropriate).

endorsements.title: Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH) guidance
endorsements.issuer: The Joint Commission and Coalition for Health AI
endorsements.quote: Explicitly prohibit the re-identification of de-identified data in data use agreements.

endorsements.title: Principles for augmented intelligence development, deployment, and use
endorsements.quote: G enerative AI tools should not reverse engineer, reconstruct, or reidentify an individual’s originally identifiable data or use identifiable data for nonpermitted uses, e.g., when data are permitted to conduct quality and safety evaluations.

endorsements.title: Use of artificial intelligence in the field of pain medicine
endorsements.quote: Furthermore, as the development of medical AI involves the processing of a substantial amount of sensitive private health-related information, obtaining appropriate legal approval for handling personal data and maintaining security is crucial.

endorsements.title: Application of artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and treatment of Kawasaki disease
endorsements.quote: Given the sensitivity of personal health information involved in AI development, obtaining appropriate legal authorization for data processing and ensuring that security measures are in place is essential.

endorsements.title: Strengthening ethics review of the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems in health research: a guide for research ethics committees in Uganda
endorsements.quote: Additionally, research institutions should negotiate data sharing agreements (DSAs) that bind both provider and recipient scientists from inappropriate access and use of individuals’ data.

endorsements.title: Open data and artificial intelligence: a window of opportunity for septic patients in emergency departments
endorsements.issuer: Emergencias : revista de la Sociedad Espanola de Medicina de Emergencias
endorsements.quote: Por ello, cualquier cesión debe estar regulada mediante acuerdos específicos, evaluaciones de impacto y supervisión continua.

endorsements.title: A call for ethical, equitable, and effective artificial intelligence to improve care for all people with epilepsy: A roadmap. A report by the ILAE Global Advocacy Council and Big Data Commission
endorsements.quote: Data collection must follow standardized procedures for informed consent, ensuring that people with epilepsy are fully aware of how their data will be used, shared, and protected.

endorsements.title: Digital infrastructures and data interoperability in radiology for prevention: from digital health to AI-enabled, quantitative imaging workflows
endorsements.quote: Implement secondary-use governance (role-based access, logging, pseudonymization workflows); separate clinical and research environments with controlled pipelines; ensure transparent patient communication and documented lawful basis/ consent pathways where relevant

commentary.bottom_line: Eight sources endorse verifying and documenting the legal basis, consent, or data use agreement for each AI data use, but no supplied study tests whether this practice reduces unlawful use or disclosure of PHI. The recommendation rests on professional consensus and legal obligation rather than on measured outcomes.

perspectives.view: No supplied study tests the practice, and no supplied study documents the hazard, so certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The eight endorsements include two frameworks, two guidance documents, and four commentaries. They agree on direction, but agreement among expert sources does not show that documentation and approval steps prevent improper disclosure.

The endorsing sources frame the practice as meeting existing legal duties. CHAI playbooks limit permitted uses to defined functions, RUAIH guidance asks that data use agreements prohibit re-identification, and the Uganda ethics guide calls for sharing agreements that bind both parties. These statements describe expected compliance, but no supplied study measures whether it reduces violations.

The ILAE roadmap states that people with epilepsy should know how their data will be used, shared, and protected. The practice may support that expectation by making each data flow traceable to a documented basis. No supplied study measures patient awareness, trust, or complaints before and after such a process.

commentary.research_gap: No study evaluates whether per-use legal basis documentation and privacy officer or data steward sign-off reduce unauthorized PHI disclosure, secondary reuse, or feedback-loop reuse in AI projects. Useful designs would compare audit findings, breach reports, or data use agreement exceptions across sites or periods with and without the approval step, and would record the review time and backlog it adds.
commentary.underserved_note: No supplied study tests the practice in any population, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients. Consent and notice processes may reach these groups differently, and whether documented consent reflects their understanding remains untested.
